q-16096.name: Question 1
q-16096.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-4$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-4$ | $-2$ | $-7$ | $1$ | $10$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=-4.$
q-16096.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-4$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=-4} & =f(-4){g}^{′}(-4)+g(-4){f}^{′}(-4) \\  & =(-2)\cdot 10+(-7)\cdot 1 \\  & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

q-104443.name: Question 2
q-104443.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
f(0)=5,\,{f}^{′}(0)=-2,\,g(0)=10,\,{g}^{′}(0)=4
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=0.$
q-104443.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=0,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=0} & =f(0){g}^{′}(0)+g(0){f}^{′}(0) \\  & =5\cdot 4+10\cdot (-2) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-104450.name: Question 3
q-104450.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(-4)=2e,\,{f}^{′}(-4)=-e,\,g(-4)=-3e,\,{g}^{′}(-4)=e
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=-4.$
q-104450.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=-4,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=-4} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-4)g(-4)-f(-4){g}^{′}(-4)}{{g}^{2}(-4)} \\  & =\frac{-e\cdot (-3e)-2e\cdot e}{9{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-48724.name: Question 4
q-48724.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(-2)=1,\,{f}^{′}(-2)=-3,\,g(-2)=2,\,{g}^{′}(-2)=6
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=-2.$
q-48724.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=-2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=-2} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-2)g(-2)-f(-2){g}^{′}(-2)}{{g}^{2}(-2)} \\  & =\frac{(-3)\cdot 2-1\cdot 6}{{2}^{2}} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

q-72999.name: Question 5
q-72999.problem:
For the functions $g(x)$ and $u(x),$ you're given the following data:

$$
g(-2)=-6,\,{g}^{′}(-2)=3,\,u(-2)=4,\,{u}^{′}(-2)=-8
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2g(x)+u(x))$ at $x=-2.$
q-72999.worked_solution:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2g(x)+u(x))=2{g}^{′}(x)+{u}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=-2$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2g(x)+u(x))|}_{x=-2} & =2{g}^{′}(-2)+{u}^{′}(-2) \\  & =2\cdot 3+(-8) \\  & =6-8 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}

$$

For the functions $e(x)$ and $n(x),$ you're given the following data:

q-311283.name: Question 9
q-311283.problem:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $t=3$ are given in the table below.

| $t$ | $h(t)$ | $z(t)$ | ${h}^{′}(t)$ | ${z}^{′}(t)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $3$ | $-2$ | $6$ | $5$ | $-1$ |

If $f(t)=\frac{2+h(t)}{z(t)},$ compute  ${f}^{′}(3).$ Do not round the answer.

${f}^{′}(3)=$
{{field-1}}
q-311283.worked_solution:
The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=2+h(t)$ and $v=z(t).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}={h}^{′}(t)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={z}^{′}(t).
$$

Substituting into the quotient rule gives

$$
{f}^{′}(t)=\frac{{h}^{′}(t)z(t)-(2+h(t)){z}^{′}(t)}{{z}^{2}(t)}.
$$

At $t=3,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =\frac{{h}^{′}(3)z(3)-(2+h(3)){z}^{′}(3)}{{z}^{2}(3)} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 6-(2+(-2))(-1)}{{6}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{30-(0)(-1)}{36} \\  & =\frac{30}{36} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
